---
title: "Interactive NBA Net Rating"
description: >
  Build the NBA offense-vs-defense quadrant in plotly with team logos and hover
  details, then a net-rating bar chart with logos on the axis, and share both
  as web pages.
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", message = FALSE,
  fig.width = 7.5, fig.height = 4.5, dpi = 96
)
```

**The brief:** the season-review blog post wants its net-rating chart to be
explorable: point at a team and read its offensive, defensive and net rating
instead of estimating them from the axes. It is the interactive version of the
[NBA Net Rating Quadrant](recipe-nba-net-rating-quadrant.html) recipe, with the
same ratings from hoopR's ESPN team box scores. The chart is built natively with
plotly's `plot_ly()`: `ggplotly()` drops sdvplotR's logo layers (see the
[interactive cookbook](cookbook-interactive.html)), so `add_sdv_logos()` places
the logos as plotly layout images instead.

```{r setup}
library(sdvplotR)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr, warn.conflicts = FALSE)
library(plotly, warn.conflicts = FALSE)

season <- 2026 # the 2025-26 season: NBA seasons are named by the year they end
label <- paste0(season - 1, "-", season %% 100)
```

## 1. Get the data

The same ratings as the static recipe: points scored and allowed per 100
possessions, with possessions estimated from the box score (FGA - OREB + TOV +
0.44 FTA) and averaged with the opponent's, so both teams in a game share one
count.

```{r data}
box <- hoopR::load_nba_team_box(season) |>
  filter(season_type == 2) # regular season

games <- box |>
  mutate(
    poss = field_goals_attempted - offensive_rebounds + total_turnovers +
      0.44 * free_throws_attempted
  )
filter(games, is.na(poss)) |>
  select(game_id, game_date, team_abbreviation, opponent_team_abbreviation)
```

One box score is missing a stat, so that game has no possession count. It is
dropped for both teams together, as in the static recipe, so no `NA` reaches
the season sums.

```{r ratings}
opponents <- select(games, game_id, opponent_team_id = team_id, opp_poss = poss)
stopifnot(identical(class(games$opponent_team_id), class(opponents$opponent_team_id)))

ratings <- games |>
  inner_join(opponents, by = c("game_id", "opponent_team_id")) |>
  mutate(game_poss = (poss + opp_poss) / 2) |>
  filter(!is.na(game_poss)) |>
  group_by(team = team_abbreviation) |>
  summarise(
    ortg = 100 * sum(team_score) / sum(game_poss),
    drtg = 100 * sum(opponent_team_score) / sum(game_poss)
  ) |>
  mutate(net = ortg - drtg)
stopifnot(!anyNA(ratings$net))
```

ESPN files the All-Star Game's teams as regular-season games, so `sdv_resolve()`
returns `NA` for them (with a warning naming the values) and they are dropped.
`sdv_teams()` adds each team's full name and conference for the hover text, and
`sdv_team_colors()` its primary color.

```{r resolve, warning = FALSE}
ratings <- ratings |>
  mutate(team_id = sdv_resolve(team, league = "nba"))
filter(ratings, is.na(team_id))$team

conferences <- sdv_teams("nba") |>
  transmute(
    team_id, team_abbr = abbr, name,
    conference = sub("ern Conference$", "", conference)
  )
ratings <- ratings |>
  filter(!is.na(team_id)) |>
  inner_join(conferences, by = "team_id") |>
  mutate(color = unname(sdv_team_colors("nba", team_abbr))) |>
  arrange(desc(net), team_abbr) |>
  mutate(tip = sprintf(
    "<b>%s</b> (%s)<br>Offensive rating: %.1f<br>Defensive rating: %.1f<br>Net rating: %+.1f",
    name, conference, ortg, drtg, net
  ))
stopifnot(nrow(ratings) == 30)
select(ratings, team_abbr, conference, ortg, drtg, net) |> head()
```

The page embeds this 30-row table, not the box scores.

## 2. Hover first

Start with the part a reader touches. A scatter trace carries one marker per
team, and `text` with `hoverinfo = "text"` replaces plotly's default hover
(raw x and y values) with the tooltip built above: name, conference and the
three ratings. `hoverlabel` colors each tooltip in the team's color. A `range`
given high-to-low reverses the axis, so the best defenses are on top, as in the
static recipe.

```{r hover, out.width = "100%"}
x_lim <- range(ratings$ortg) + c(-1, 1)
y_lim <- range(ratings$drtg) + c(-1, 1)

plot_ly(
  ratings, x = ~ortg, y = ~drtg, type = "scatter", mode = "markers",
  marker = list(size = 12, color = ~color),
  text = ~tip, hoverinfo = "text",
  hoverlabel = list(bgcolor = ~color, font = list(color = "white"))
) |>
  layout(
    title = list(text = paste("NBA offense vs defense,", label, "regular season"), x = 0.02),
    xaxis = list(title = "Offensive rating (points per 100 possessions)", range = x_lim),
    yaxis = list(title = "Defensive rating (allowed per 100)", range = rev(y_lim))
  )
```

The dots already answer "who is that?", but a reader still has to hover each
one to find a team.

## 3. Logos, average lines and net-rating guides

`add_sdv_logos()` puts each team's logo at its point, in data units. Its `size`
is the logo height as a share of the y-axis span. The markers stay as the hover
targets, now transparent (`opacity = 0`), and plotly has no geom for reference
lines, so they go in as layout `shapes`. Dashed lines mark the league-average
offense and defense, and the faint diagonals are the static recipe's net-rating
guides: teams on one line share a net rating, in steps of 5. Each diagonal is
cut to the axis box first.

```{r guides}
# the line drtg = ortg - net, cut to the box x_lim by y_lim
guides <- data.frame(net = c(-10, -5, 0, 5, 10)) |>
  mutate(
    x0 = pmax(x_lim[1], y_lim[1] + net),
    x1 = pmin(x_lim[2], y_lim[2] + net)
  ) |>
  filter(x0 < x1) |>
  mutate(
    y0 = x0 - net, y1 = x1 - net,
    lx = x0 + 0.88 * (x1 - x0), ly = lx - net, # a label near the lower-right end
    label = if_else(net > 0, paste0("+", net), as.character(net))
  )

line_shape <- function(x0, y0, x1, y1, color, dash = "solid") {
  list(
    type = "line", x0 = x0, y0 = y0, x1 = x1, y1 = y1, layer = "below",
    line = list(color = color, width = 1, dash = dash)
  )
}
shapes <- c(
  Map(line_shape, guides$x0, guides$y0, guides$x1, guides$y1, "#e0e0e0"),
  list(
    line_shape(mean(ratings$ortg), y_lim[1], mean(ratings$ortg), y_lim[2], "#999999", "dash"),
    line_shape(x_lim[1], mean(ratings$drtg), x_lim[2], mean(ratings$drtg), "#999999", "dash")
  )
)
guide_labels <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(guides)), function(i) {
  list(
    x = guides$lx[i], y = guides$ly[i], text = guides$label[i],
    showarrow = FALSE, font = list(color = "#999999", size = 10)
  )
})
```

```{r quadrant, out.width = "100%"}
quadrant <- plot_ly(
  ratings, x = ~ortg, y = ~drtg, type = "scatter", mode = "markers",
  marker = list(size = 30, opacity = 0),
  text = ~tip, hoverinfo = "text",
  hoverlabel = list(bgcolor = ~color, font = list(color = "white"))
) |>
  layout(
    title = list(
      text = paste0(
        "NBA offense vs defense, ", label, " regular season",
        "<br><sup>Up and right is better. Dashed: league average. Diagonals: net rating.</sup>"
      ),
      x = 0.02
    ),
    xaxis = list(title = "Offensive rating (points per 100 possessions)", range = x_lim, zeroline = FALSE),
    yaxis = list(title = "Defensive rating (allowed per 100)", range = rev(y_lim), zeroline = FALSE),
    shapes = shapes, annotations = guide_labels,
    margin = list(t = 70)
  ) |>
  add_sdv_logos(ratings$ortg, ratings$drtg, ratings$team_abbr, "nba", size = 0.07)
quadrant
```

Hovering works as before, since the transparent markers sit where the logos
are. plotly's toolbar adds zoom: drag a box around the crowded middle of the
chart and the logos spread apart; double-click to zoom back out.

## 4. Net rating as bars, logos on the axis

The quadrant shows two numbers per team; a bar chart ranks the one that sums
them up. Order the teams by net rating with a factor, color each bar in its
team's color, and `sdv_axis_logos()` replaces the category labels with logos
(it hides the tick labels and puts a logo under each bar). `textposition =
"none"` keeps the hover text out of the bars.

```{r bars, out.width = "100%"}
bars <- ratings |>
  mutate(team_abbr = factor(team_abbr, levels = team_abbr)) # already sorted by net rating

plot_ly(
  bars, x = ~team_abbr, y = ~net, type = "bar",
  marker = list(color = ~color),
  text = ~tip, hoverinfo = "text", textposition = "none",
  hoverlabel = list(bgcolor = ~color, font = list(color = "white"))
) |>
  layout(
    title = list(text = paste("NBA net rating,", label, "regular season"), x = 0.02),
    xaxis = list(title = ""),
    yaxis = list(title = "Net rating (points per 100 possessions)"),
    margin = list(t = 50, b = 50)
  ) |>
  sdv_axis_logos(levels(bars$team_abbr), "nba")
```

## 5. Share it

`htmlwidgets::saveWidget()` writes a chart to one HTML file, and
`selfcontained = TRUE` inlines plotly's JavaScript so no folder sits beside it
(it needs pandoc, which ships with RStudio). plotly's logos are layout images
that load from their URLs, so the file is small but needs the network when it
is opened.

```{r save-html}
out <- tempfile("sdvplotR-recipe-")
dir.create(out)
html <- file.path(out, "nba_net_rating_interactive.html")
htmlwidgets::saveWidget(quadrant, html, selfcontained = TRUE, title = "NBA offense vs defense")
round(file.size(html) / 1024) # kilobytes, most of it plotly.js
```

## 6. The static version

plotly has no `ggsave()`, and a screenshot of the widget needs a headless
browser (the cookbook's last recipe shows it with webshot2). For a post or a
slide, draw the static recipe's ggplot instead, from the same `ratings` and
`guides` tables: `geom_sdv_logos()` for the logos, `geom_mean_lines()` for each
conference's averages, and a panel per conference.

```{r export, fig.alt = "Static two-panel chart of NBA offensive against defensive rating by conference, 2025-26, with team logos, dashed conference-average lines, faint diagonals marking net ratings from -10 to +10, and the defensive axis reversed so up and right is better."}
ggplot(ratings, aes(ortg, drtg)) +
  geom_segment(
    aes(x = x0, y = y0, xend = x1, yend = y1),
    data = guides, inherit.aes = FALSE, color = "grey88", linewidth = 0.4
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(x = lx, y = ly, label = label),
    data = guides, inherit.aes = FALSE, color = "grey60", size = 2.6
  ) +
  geom_mean_lines(aes(x0 = ortg, y0 = drtg), color = "grey60", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_sdv_logos(aes(team = team_abbr), league = "nba", width = 0.1) +
  facet_wrap(vars(conference)) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = 0.06)) +
  scale_y_reverse(expand = expansion(mult = 0.08)) +
  labs(
    title = paste("NBA offense vs defense,", label, "regular season"),
    subtitle = "Up and right is better. Dashed: conference average. Diagonals: net rating.",
    x = "Offensive rating (points per 100 possessions)",
    y = "Defensive rating (allowed per 100)",
    caption = "Data: ESPN via hoopR  |  Chart: sdvplotR"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    plot.title.position = "plot",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "grey40", size = 9),
    plot.caption = element_text(color = "grey45", size = 7.5),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11, hjust = 0),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )
```
